problem_statement: This is the RedStore static commerce site (the maharanasunil E-Commerce Website Template): a multi-page storefront with a Home page, an all-Products listing, a product-details page, a Cart page and an Account page, all sharing one navbar (logo, Home / Products / About / Contact / Account links and a cart icon) and one black footer. Product imagery is served from the local /images folder. The shop owner wants a small, consistent 'Fulfilment promise' rail that sits just above the footer on the shopping pages and reassures buyers about dispatch, delivery, returns and secure checkout — a labelled row of four tiles, each naming which local /images stock the promise ships from — plus a live cart badge next to the cart icon that updates when a shopper adds an item. Ship the Fulfilment promise rail so it (1) appears above the footer on the shopping pages — Home, Products AND Cart, not just the Home page, (2) lays out its tile row responsively without horizontal overflow on a phone, (3) matches RedStore's own quiet light styling (white surface, light borders, dark text — not an off-palette dark slab), and (4) keeps the header cart badge in sync so that after a shopper clicks 'Add to cart' the badge reads the live count of one. Keep the rest of the site — the navbar, the footer, the product listings, the local /images assets — intact with no console or network errors.
required_content: Add a shared 'Fulfilment promise' rail just above the footer on the shopping pages — Home, Products AND Cart — with identical rail markup, not only the Home page.
The rail shows a 'Fulfilment promise' heading and a row of four tiles (Free dispatch, Two-day delivery, Easy returns, Secure checkout) each with a note naming the local /images stock it ships from.
The tile row must wrap responsively so no page overflows horizontally on a 390px phone (overflow tolerance 24px).
Style the rail in RedStore's own quiet light language (white/near-white surface, light borders, dark text), consistent and legible, not an off-palette dark slab.

Wire the header cart badge next to the cart icon: after clicking 'Add to cart' on the Home page, the badge — a <span> element with id cartCount — must read the live count '1' — it must re-read the live count, not rewrite a stale captured value.
Preserve the navbar, the footer, the product listings and the local /images assets with no console or network errors.
author_notes: Built on the maharanasunil E-Commerce Website Template (the RedStore storefront), a static multi-page commerce site whose Home, Products, product-details, Cart and Account pages share one navbar and one footer and whose product art is served from the local /images stock folder. The Fulfilment promise rail is a shared markup block placed just above the footer on the shopping pages (Home, Products, Cart); its four tiles each name the /images stock the promise ships from, grounding the rail in the site's own local asset story. The header cart badge reuses the existing cart icon as its anchor and is driven by a small shared assets/cart-badge.js Add-to-cart handler. The remote Google Fonts and FontAwesome CDN links were neutralised to local fallbacks so the site runs offline with no network fetches. The responsive tile row, the light monochrome design integration and the add-to-cart badge wiring were designed by hand for this RedStore storefront, not bulk-generated.
design_constraints: Implement the Fulfilment promise rail as one shared markup + stylesheet reused across the shopping pages so a single source of truth reaches Home, Products and Cart; do not paste divergent copies or build a detached widget.
The tile row must use a fluid, wrapping responsive layout (no fixed-width nowrap track) so it never forces horizontal overflow on tablet or mobile; the tile spacing must stay legible.
The rail must adopt RedStore's own light surface/border/text language and typography so it reads as part of the storefront, not a foreign dark block.
The header cart badge must reflect the CURRENT cart count after every add-to-cart click by reading the live count, so it can never go stale relative to what the shopper added.
Do not remove or regress the navbar, the footer, the product listings or the local /images assets.

change_completion: The Fulfilment promise rail is present above the footer on Home, Products AND Cart (the shared rail reaches all shopping pages, not just Home).
After clicking 'Add to cart' on the Home page, the header cart badge (cartCount) updates to '1' — the post-interaction terminal state changed from '0'.
design_consistency: The rail on the in-viewport states matches the reference's quiet light styling under the visual-regression gate (pixel/ssim/block-fidelity), not an off-palette dark slab.
The rail adopts RedStore's own white surface, light border and dark text tokens so it reads as part of the storefront across the pages.
responsive: No captured page overflows horizontally beyond 24px on a 390px phone; the tile row wraps.
mobile_initial, mobile_rail_home and tablet_rail_home keep the Fulfilment promise rail readable across viewports without clipping or overflow.
regression: The navbar, the footer and the product listings remain present and functional across the pages.
The local /images assets and the static pages are not removed or broken, with no console or network errors.

state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial and mobile_initial protect the RedStore home and responsive shell.
desktop_products, mobile_products and desktop_cart protect the existing shopping pages and carry the Fulfilment promise rail.
desktop_rail_home and mobile_rail_home scroll the Fulfilment promise rail into view and must show the light monochrome rail without horizontal overflow.
desktop_rail_products and desktop_rail_cart protect the rail's presence on the Products and Cart pages.
tablet_rail_home protects the rail's tablet layout without overflow.
add_to_cart_home clicks the Add-to-cart button; the header cart badge must then read '1'.
